messages:
jordana: heads-up — seeing nondeterministic outputs from the eval runner on CI for the quantized model bringup. same seed + config but different samples across retries. repro id run-20260320-001 :thinking_face:

sam: ugh, another seeding flake? which sampling params diverge (temp/top_p)?

jordana: mostly top_p=0.9 runs, but some temp=0.0 runs also differ. differences show up only when we run with >1 worker and streaming enabled. single-worker runs are stable.

kai: pinging in — my hunch is RNG reuse across worker tasks. we've seen worker-pool recycling leave shared RNG instances in the past. are we seeding per-request or per-worker?

jordana: currently we do `seed = base_seed + shard_id` at worker startup and reuse that RNG for the whole worker lifetime. code snippet from runner: 
```
# simplified
worker_seed = base_seed + shard_id
rng = np.random.default_rng(worker_seed)
for req in worker.loop:
    samples = sampler.sample(rng, ...)
```
This worked when runs were short, but long evals with streaming + resume paths seem to interleave RNG calls.

olivia-qa: observed flake pattern in CI: 3/20 runs failed by >1 token mismatch on canonical prompts, mostly when run parallelism >= 4. adding checksum diff in harness flagged it.

sam: ok, we should avoid long-lived shared RNGs. options: per-request RNG derived from (base_seed, request_id) deterministic HMAC, or make RNG usage single-threaded via fine-grained lock. HMAC approach is nice because it produces independent, deterministic streams. e.g.
```
# per-request RNG proposal
def make_rng(base_seed: int, request_id: str):
    key = hmac_sha256(str(base_seed).encode(), request_id.encode())
    seed_int = int.from_bytes(key[:8], 'big')
    return np.random.default_rng(seed_int)
```

kai: agree. locks will work but can degrade throughput under high concurrency. per-request RNG is safer. also ensure sampler uses only rng.sample(...) deterministically and doesn't call global randoms.

jordana: I'll prototype HMAC-per-request RNG and add a small stress test that spawns 1000 concurrent requests and asserts identical outputs across 3 retries.

olivia-qa: can we also add a CI gate that runs a 10x quick stochastic check on PRs touching runner/sampler? even a short 50-case check would catch regressions early.

sam: yes — plan: (1) quick unit test for seed determinism, (2) stress job in nightly for larger parallelism, (3) add checksum diff metric to the eval report and fail PR if >X mismatches.

jordana: landed a draft patch to branch `eng-ml/seed-fix` with the HMAC RNG and a deterministic checksum. small diff attached in PR. will add unit tests shortly.

ci-bot: flaky-test-detector: detected 3 failures in last 2 hours for pipeline `eval-runner-e2e`. marking as flaky=possible. see https://ci.redwood.ai/build/ev-20260320-9

sam: thanks for the link. @jordana when you push tests ping me and i'll help add the CI gate wiring.

jordana: pushed tests, added `tests/eval/test_seed_determinism.py` + a quick stress harness. diff includes new util `make_rng` and replaces worker-global rng usage.

olivia-qa: quick run on my laptop (4 cores) — 100 concurrent requests x 3 retries — all identical outputs. :tada:

ci-bot: CI: rerun of PR eng-ml/seed-fix — 5/5 e2e runs passed (quick-stress subset).

sam: nice. next: rolling this into nightly and enable checksum gating at 0.5% mismatch threshold. we'll monitor for perf regressions from creating per-request RNGs.

jordana: noted. will benchmark overhead; early numbers look minimal since RNG construction is just a few ops. will follow up with perf numbers in this thread. :eyes:
